newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden govt still sees unemployment halved in 2000.
newsitem.headline: Sweden govt still sees unemployment halved in 2000.

text.p: The Swedish government said on Tuesday it expected to be able to keep its pledge to halve unemployment to four percent in the year 2000.

"The conditions are good for reaching the goal to halve unemployment to the year 2000," Finance Minister Erik Asbrink told a press conference after the government presented its spring budget proposal.
But in the proposal, the government forecast unemployment of 4.5 percent in 2000, down from March 1997 levels of 8.4 percent.
"In the autumn budget proposal the forecast was for unemployment to be 5.7 percent in 2000," Asbrink said.

"Now (in the spring budget proposal) the figure has been pushed down by another 50,000 so it remains for us to reduce the number of unemployed by another 20,000 to reach four percent. We have three years to introduce further measures if needed."
In its budget proposal, the government forecast unemployment falling from 7.9 percent in 1997 to 7.1 percent in 1998, and 5.6 percent in 1999.
